# CAS Handbook: How to Play
## Aerial Support & Deployment Platforms
This handbook explains the gameplay controls for fitting, loading, targeting, and firing dropship weapons. It is not an SOP, rules-of-engagement document, or UCMJ reference.
Dropships provide troop transport and Close Air Support (CAS). The available craft and attachment points depend on the map: examples include the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color], [color=#808080]Normandy[/color], Fallujah, and Mohawk.
[bold]Both the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color] and [color=#808080]Normandy[/color] are engineered to perform essential troop transport and devastating Close Air Support (CAS) missions[/bold], adapting to the dynamic needs of any operation.
This guide will cover the general aspects of troop transport, attachment overview and then provide a more in-depth look at executing effective Close Air Support.
## I. Troop Transport: Lifeline to the Front
Efficient troop transport is vital. While both dropships can ferry marines, the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color] is often designated as the primary workhorse for shuttling squads and supplies between The Almayer and The Main LZ.
### Optimizing Your Transport Runs:
- [bold]Destination Selection:[/bold] Use the navigation console to select an available landing destination before launching. Transport travel and CAS fly-by runs are different flight modes. - [bold]Departure Callouts:[/bold] Be sure to announce departure times on [color=#808080]common ship radio[/color] to reduce the chance of leaving any marine behind on ship. - [bold]Have the Pilot Fly:[/bold] Having [color=#FFFF00]Piloting Skill 2[/color] (standard for Dropship/Gunship Pilots and ASOs) [color=#ADD8E6]reduces dropship refuel time by 25%[/color]. [bold]This stacks with the Cooling System.[/bold]
## II. Dropship Armaments & Engine Attachments
The CAS interface supports up to [bold]seven weapons[/bold], including weapons on internal points. This does not add attachment points to a craft: your actual loadout is limited by the exterior, engine, and interior points on its map. An interior weapon occupies a point that could otherwise hold a utility module.
### Preparing a Loadout
1. Print the weapon and its matching ammunition from the Dropship Part Fabricator. 2. Use a powerloader to move and install heavy weapon attachments on compatible points. 3. Load heavy GAU crates, laser batteries, and rocket packs with a powerloader. Match the ammunition to the installed weapon. 4. For BOFORS and Howitzer ammunition, take an individual magazine or shell from its tray or rack with [bold]both hands free[/bold], then click the weapon's attachment point to load it. Click the point with an empty hand to unload it. The whole tray or rack is a transport container, not the fired ammunition. 5. Open [bold]Equip[/bold] on the weapons console to check the installed weapon, loaded payload, and ammunition before flying.
Exterior powerloader loading is blocked while the dropship is in flight. Interior BOFORS and Howitzer mounts can be serviced by hand from the cabin; use them if you want to reload without returning to a landing pad.
### A. Weapon Systems
Exterior Bofors and Howitzer mounts on the Fallujah and Mohawk display the full weapon frame, whether loaded or empty. Interior mounts retain their separate loaded and unloaded artwork.
Interior-mounted Bofors, Howitzer, and JDAM bomb clamps are listed alongside exterior weapons. When more than four weapons are installed, use the [bold]PREVIOUS[/bold] and [bold]NEXT[/bold] buttons at the bottom of the equipment, strike weapon, or firemission editor screen to browse the weapon pages.

These GAU crates hold [bold]400 rounds[/bold] and spend [bold]40 rounds per trigger[/bold]: ten full bursts per crate. One trigger starts a burst, not a single bullet.
[bold]Building a mixed GAU belt[/bold]: 1. Print an empty mixed ammunition belt carrier. 2. With a powerloader, use a GAU crate on the carrier. Repeat for up to three crates; they fill slots 1, 2, and 3 in order. 3. Install the carrier in the GAU's ammunition point instead of a single crate. 4. Each trigger fires one whole burst from the next slot: 1, then 2, then 3, then back to 1. Empty slots and crates with fewer than 40 rounds are skipped. A full three-crate carrier supplies thirty bursts. 5. Examine the carrier to inspect the slot order. Use its slot eject verbs to remove crates and change the loadout.
Mixing does not blend damage types inside a burst. [bold]Next burst[/bold] in the console identifies the next crate's payload; [bold]Bursts left[/bold] counts usable bursts across the carrier. The same sequence is used by direct CAS triggers and fire missions. Different GAU ammunition types cannot refill one another, and a carrier cannot be refilled by combining it with another carrier.
- [bold]Overview[/bold]: An area denial weapon that projects a laser to create a field of intense, albeit short-lived fires. - [bold]Firing Window[/bold]: Can be used during [color=#00FF00]Transit AND Fly-by runs[/color]. - [bold]Ammunition & Characteristics[/bold]:
The cannon randomly covers a [color=#FFA500]7x7 area with 16 total fires[/color]. These fires have a very short duration but are of very high intensity, making them ideal for flushing enemies or temporary area denial. The ammunition is very cost-efficient, with a full reload providing 10 shots. It boasts the [color=#ADD8E6]fastest travel time of any CAS weapon (1 second)[/color] and has a minimal [color=#FFD700]1-tile inaccuracy[/color].
[bold]Green "Verdant"[/bold]: Wider green fire coverage; twenty triggers per battery.
[bold]Blue "Glacier"[/bold]: Concentrated blue fire coverage; five triggers per battery.
[bold]White "Daybreak"[/bold]: White-hot fire with a small footprint and high charge consumption; two triggers per battery.
[bold]Rapidfire[/bold]: Five simultaneous laser pulses per trigger, each igniting its own impact area. A full battery provides [bold]ten triggers[/bold], for fifty pulse impacts in total. It still uses the laser cannon's firing cooldown.
[bold]Changing the Rapidfire pattern[/bold]: Select the loaded laser cannon on either monitor, then click its pattern button to switch between [bold]Laser: wide ring[/bold] and [bold]Laser: sweeping line[/bold]. - [bold]Wide ring[/bold]: Five points around the aimpoint, six tiles from the center. There is no central pulse. - [bold]Sweeping line[/bold]: Five points across a twelve-tile line, including a central pulse. Both patterns follow the dropship's orientation and have the same charge cost. Check the preview before firing. Changing the pattern affects future shots, not pulses already released.
[bold]L/60 40mm BOFORS (ATC)[/bold]: Fits exterior weapon points and interior weapon-capable utility points. Each magazine holds twenty rounds; a trigger consumes five, providing [bold]four bursts per magazine[/bold]. All five ammunition types use genuine explosions, not GAU-style direct tile hits. - [bold]HE[/bold]: General explosive bombardment. - [bold]AP[/bold]: Penetrates cover before a focused explosive detonation. - [bold]Airburst[/bold]: Wider anti-infantry coverage, with selectable burst height. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: A concentrated anti-armor explosive payload. - [bold]Incendiary[/bold]: Explosive impacts that also start fires.
[bold]Changing BOFORS airburst height[/bold]: Load an Airburst magazine, select the BOFORS on the console, and click the height button to cycle [bold]low, medium, and high[/bold]. Medium is the default. Low concentrates the blast into fewer tiles at higher intensity; high spreads the same explosive energy over more tiles at lower intensity. The preview updates with the setting.
These are detonation-height gameplay profiles above the target, [bold]not a selector for a building floor or z-level[/bold]. The setting is only available for BOFORS Airburst ammunition, requires the weapon's pilot skill, and affects future shots only.
[bold]M137 105mm Howitzer (HWR)[/bold]: Fits exterior and interior points and holds one physical shell at a time. Load a fresh shell after firing. - [bold]HE[/bold]: Heavy explosive damage against positions. - [bold]HE-FRAG[/bold]: Explosive fragmentation coverage. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: Anti-armor bombardment. - [bold]HE Airburst[/bold]: Multiple dispersed explosive impacts from one physical shell. It does not use the BOFORS height selector.
[bold]JDAM Bomb Clamp (BMB)[/bold]: Fits interior crew-compartment points only and holds one JDAM-family bomb. Use a powerloader to install the clamp and load its matching bomb into the point. HE provides a large blast; Incendiary adds fire; AP emphasizes penetration; Cluster disperses bomblets; Napalm blankets an area in fire. A cluster payload's displayed bomblet count does not mean the clamp holds several bombs.
BOFORS, Howitzer, and the bomb clamp use the normal CAS firing workflow and require a fly-by rather than ordinary transport transit. [bold]An internal mount allows cabin servicing; it does not turn a CAS weapon into a landed turret.[/bold]

Payloads differ in charge consumption, dispersion, and effects. Read the selected ammunition and remaining triggers instead of assuming every pack fires the same way.
### B. Engine Attachments These modules are fitted to dedicated engine attachment points to enhance dropship performance.
[color=#ADD8E6]Reduces overall travel time[/color] AND [color=#ADD8E6]increases available fly-by time by 25%[/color]. Excellent for rapid response, quicker transport cycles, and extended CAS presence.
[color=#ADD8E6]Significantly reduces dropship refuel time by 50%[/color], decreasing downtime at The Almayer or LZ. - [bold]Stacking Note[/bold]: Both engine attachments can be equipped simultaneously, and their effects stack, but with diminishing returns. The Pilot skill bonus also stacks with the Cooling System.
### C. Internal Utility Modules Dropships feature [bold]3 utility point[/bold], located inside the dropship near the rear. These mounts can be fitted with specialized modules to enhance the dropship's support capabilities. Currently, two primary utility modules are available:
- When this module is installed, the dropship gains the ability to [color=#ADD8E6]retrieve items or corpses that have been sent up from the ground via a fulton[/color]. The Pilot has to use their console to recover the fultonned items
- Equipping this module allows the dropship to [color=#00FF00]recover critically wounded or downed personnel on medevac stretcher directly from the battlefield[/color]. - To recover personnel with the medevac system, the pilot must first select the medevac system from the weapons console and has to manually interact with the medevac to activate it. The medevac system also has a 20 second cooldown - [bold][color=#FF0000]Vital for casualty evacuation. Remember to tend to the recovered personnel and inform medical on their status, do not leave them unattended after landing at the Almayer.[/color][/bold]
### D. Acquiring Armaments & Attachments (Dropship Fabricator) All weapon systems, their respective ammunition, and engine attachments are not freely available. They must be acquired through a Dropship Part Fabricator found above the landing pads
uses a system of [color=#FFFF00]"Dropship Points"[/color] to print these items. - [bold]Replenishing Dropship Points[/bold]: There are two primary ways to obtain or replenish these crucial dropship points:
1. [bold]Passive Regeneration[/bold]: Dropship points regenerate passively over time, but at a [color=#FFA500]very slow rate[/color] (approximately 1 point every 3 seconds). This method is often insufficient for rapid re-arming during active operations.
2. [bold]Command Intervention[/bold]: [color=#FFD700]The most effective and timely way to replenish spent dropship points is through Command intervention.[/color] Command staff can spend [color=#00FF00]"Intel Points"[/color] to purchase dropship points, which are then credited to the dropship systems for immediate fabrication of armaments and attachments.
- Check each item's point cost before printing. Running out of points prevents further fabrication until the balance is replenished.
## A. Accessing & Understanding the CAS Interface
Every aspect of a CAS run is controlled via the [bold]Weapons Controls Console[/bold]. - [bold]Dual Monitors:[/bold] Once the console is open, you will see two monitors. Both monitors can display the same selection of windows and operate independently, allowing you to have two different informational or control windows open simultaneously (Target on one, Cams on the other) - [bold]Available Buttons:[/bold] The primary windows accessible on these monitors are: [bold]Equip[/bold], [bold]Target[/bold], and [bold]Cams[/bold].
### B. Navigating the Weapon Control Buttons 1. [bold]The "Equip"[/bold] - Provides a detailed overview of the dropship's current loadout. - It shows what kind of weapon systems are attached to the dropship's weapon slots and displays the type and remaining quantity of ammunition for each installed weapon.
2. [bold]The "Cams"[/bold] - Provides a camera view centered on the selected target and its immediate surroundings. - When this window is active, it will display the visual feed from the area around the target currently selected. [bold]Camera Control[/bold]: - Located [italic]between the two main monitor windows[/italic], you will find four directional arrows. - Using these arrows allows you to [color=#ADD8E6]slightly move the camera view around[/color] the selected target point. You can use the button in the center to reset the camera back to the target. - [color=#FFD700][bold]Important Note[/bold][/color]: Selecting a different camera subject does not change the strike target, but the directional arrows change the console's shared offset. Direct CAS strikes land at the selected strike target plus that offset. Check the targeting preview and reset the offset when you no longer need it.
3. [bold]The "Target"[/bold] - This is your primary interface for selecting targets and firing the dropship's weapon systems. [bold]Firing Sequence - Step-by-Step:[/bold] - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select Target[/bold][/color]: You must choose a target. On the right side of the "Target" window, a list of available targets will be displayed. These targets are typically those designated by ground teams using [color=#FF0000]Laser Designators[/color] or [color=#00FF00]Signal Flares[/color]. Click on the desired target to select it. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select "Strike"[/bold][/color]: Once a target is selected, press the "Strike" button within the window. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select "Weapon"[/bold][/color]: This will bring up a list showing all equipped weapon systems. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Choose Your Weapon[/bold][/color]: Select the specific weapon system you intend to fire at the chosen target. - [bold]Check the preview and payload settings[/bold]: With a weapon and valid target selected, the strike/weapon view can display the target camera with an overlay. Check the next burst, remaining bursts, and any laser-pattern or airburst-height setting. - [color=#FF0000][bold]Select "Fire"[/bold][/color]: Confirm your selections by pressing the "Fire" button. - [bold]If the sequence was performed correctly, you should hear the distinct sound of the selected weapon firing.[/bold]
[bold]Weapon Cooldowns & Rapid Fire:[/bold] - Individual weapons have a [italic]short internal cooldown[/italic] before they can be fired again. - However, there is [bold]no hard delay between firing -different- guns[/bold]. This means once one weapon has fired (example GAU-21), you can immediately repeat the "Strike" -> "Weapon" (select a different GAU-21 or another weapon) -> "Fire" sequence to unleash another salvo with a different weapon system very quickly. This allows for potent combined-arms attacks.
### C. Reading Targeting Previews
- [bold]Yellow outlines[/bold] show the estimated payload footprint. For a Rapidfire battery, the five separate outlines show its five impact areas. - [bold]Orange outlines[/bold] show the dispersion envelope around the target. They are not a guarantee that every tile inside the outline will be damaged. - Blast previews use an unobstructed estimate. Walls, overhead cover, penetration, blast resistance, and tile snapping affect actual impacts. Fire footprints can contain gaps. - A camera can observe a different target from the selected strike target. [bold]Changing camera subjects alone does not select a new strike target.[/bold] - The shared directional-arrow [bold]offset does affect direct CAS aim[/bold]: a direct strike uses the selected target plus that offset. Reset it with the center button. During a fire mission, the mission's vector and per-weapon step offsets control the pass.
### D. Fire Missions
Open [bold]Fire Mission[/bold] to create and name a mission, then use its editor to select weapons and assign offsets at the available timing steps. A blank offset means that weapon will not fire at that step. Use weapon-page buttons to reach internal mounts or additional guns.
Choose the mission from the strike menu, select a designated target, choose the strike vector, and fire. The mission advances along that vector and releases the scheduled weapons at their steps. Check the ammunition totals before starting; mixed GAU belts advance one crate per scheduled burst.
### E. Mohawk Groundside Chin Turret
The fixed twin 90mm M90 chin gun has a [bold]180-degree forward arc[/bold] and a [bold]30-tile range[/bold]. While landed, it automatically engages visible hostiles using the craft's existing faction/IFF rules and fires individual HEAP shells. Groundside turret operation is disabled during takeoff or hovering; airborne CAS uses the weapon's burst behavior instead.
[bold]Manual aiming[/bold]: 1. Buckle into the Mohawk's gunnery seat and open the dedicated gunnery console. 2. Press [bold]Take turret control[/bold]. This suspends the default automatic targeting. 3. Use the left camera view to aim and click to fire. Combat-mode firing in the main view is also supported. 4. The overlay shows the forward arc, range, and aim marker. Red indicates an out-of-range/out-of-arc aimpoint or confirmed tracked engagement; green indicates an aimpoint inside the arc and range. It does not guarantee an unobstructed shot.
[bold]Tracking a moving hostile[/bold]: 1. While in manual control, press [bold]Mark hostile[/bold], then click a visible hostile in the left camera view. 2. The camera follows the target and displays its range. Marking alone does [bold]not[/bold] fire. 3. Continue firing manually, or press [bold]CONFIRM automatic fire[/bold] to authorize repeated fire at that marked target. 4. Press [bold]Stop / clear tracking[/bold] to stop tracked engagement and return to manual aiming. Clicking the left camera to fire manually also clears tracking.
A dead, friendly, obscured, out-of-range, or rear-arc target loses its lock and automatic-fire confirmation. Mark and confirm again to resume. Running out of ammunition stops confirmed engagement. Closing the console, leaving the gunnery seat, or leaving the landed state releases manual control.
[bold]Restore automatic control[/bold] returns the turret to its default landed IFF targeting. Closing the console also restores that default behavior: it is [bold]not[/bold] a persistent hold-fire command.
### F. Gameplay Troubleshooting
- [bold]Weapon missing from the list[/bold]: Check whether it is installed on a compatible point, then browse the weapon pages. A dedicated direct-fire-only weapon is not a normal CAS selection. - [bold]Cannot load[/bold]: Match the ammunition to the weapon, clear the occupied ammunition slot, and use the correct method: powerloader for heavy packs, both hands free for individual hand-loaded rounds. - [bold]Cannot fire[/bold]: Read the popup. Check flight mode, pilot skill, cooldown, loaded ammunition, and whether a fire mission is already active. Most CAS weapons cannot fire while landed. - [bold]Target disappeared[/bold]: Have the ground player designate again, then reselect the target. - [bold]Strike rejected under cover[/bold]: Select ammunition with suitable overhead penetration. Dispersion can move an impact beneath protected cover even when the central target is valid. - [bold]Belt still has rounds but will not fire[/bold]: Every remaining crate may contain fewer than forty rounds. Leftover rounds from different crates are not combined into a burst. - [bold]Pattern/height button missing[/bold]: Pattern selection requires a Rapidfire laser battery; height selection requires a BOFORS Airburst magazine. - [bold]Turret will not track[/bold]: Take control from the gunnery seat while landed. The mark must be a visible IFF-hostile inside the forward arc and range.
### G. Practical Gameplay Tips
- [bold]Use both monitors[/bold]: Keep "Target" open for firing and "Cams" or "Equip" open for observation or ammunition checks. - [bold]Account for travel time[/bold]: The target can move between release and impact. Fast laser strikes and slower missiles or bombs require different lead distances. - [bold]Monitor ammunition[/bold]: Check the loaded payload and full bursts remaining before starting a mission. - [bold]Switch weapons during cooldowns[/bold]: Another ready weapon can fire while the first weapon cools down. - [bold]Reset offsets when changing tasks[/bold]: A forgotten direct-fire offset shifts subsequent strikes away from their designation. - [bold]Check the actual aimpoint[/bold]: Ordinary CAS uses the selected strike target plus the console offset, not an arbitrary camera subject. The manually controlled Mohawk chin turret instead uses your click in its left camera view. - [bold]Allow room for scatter and fire[/bold]: CAS explosions and burning tiles can damage nearby allies. The preview is an estimate, not a friendly-fire barrier. - [bold]Match the payload to the job[/bold]: Use precision or AP payloads for focused targets, fragmentation for exposed groups, and incendiaries for persistent area denial.
